definitions.gloss: aerial bombing; air strike; bombing from the air
definitions.explanation: An attack in which bombs are dropped from aircraft onto targets on the ground. A concise, modern term commonly used in news reporting.

examples.japanese: {軍事|ぐんじ}{施設|しせつ}が{空爆|くうばく}された。
examples.english: Military facilities were bombed from the air.

examples.japanese: {空爆|くうばく}で{民間人|みんかんじん}にも{被害|ひがい}が{出|で}ている。
examples.english: Civilians are also being harmed by the air strikes.

examples.japanese: {国連|こくれん}は{空爆|くうばく}の{即時|そくじ}{停止|ていし}を{求|もと}める{声明|せいめい}を{発表|はっぴょう}した。
examples.english: The United Nations issued a statement demanding an immediate halt to the air strikes.

notes:
Composed of {空|くう} (sky, air) and {爆|ばく} (bomb, explosion). A modern, concise term favored in news headlines and contemporary reporting. Also functions as a する verb: {空爆|くうばく}する (to bomb from the air).

USAGE:
The standard term in contemporary news for describing military air strikes. More concise and modern-sounding than {爆撃|ばくげき} or {空襲|くうしゅう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空爆|くうばく}する — to carry out an air strike
- {空爆|くうばく}を{受|う}ける — to be hit by an air strike
- {空爆|くうばく}を{中止|ちゅうし}する — to halt air strikes
- {無差別|むさべつ}{空爆|くうばく} — indiscriminate bombing

RELATED WORDS:
- {空襲|くうしゅう} — air raid; more historical, strongly associated with WWII
- {爆撃|ばくげき} — bombing; the general military term for dropping bombs
- {砲撃|ほうげき} — shelling; artillery fire from the ground
